data.long_meaning: The one who owns or possesses. This name is derived from the Prophet Zaid ibn Harithah (ra), who was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh).

data.cultural_impact: The name Zaid is rooted in the rich history of the Islamic civilization, specifically in the life of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and his companions. Zaid ibn Harithah (ra) was an early convert to Islam and an influential figure during the early Islamic community. His name became a symbol of ownership and possession in the Islamic culture, representing one's commitment to and ownership of the Islamic faith and the values it upholds.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Zaid holds spiritual significance as it is derived from the noble character of Prophet Zaid ibn Harithah (ra). He was a devoted and loyal servant of Allah, and his name serves as a reminder to uphold the spiritual virtues of faith, commitment, and devotion to Allah. It is a reminder that all belongings, including one's faith, should be held in the name of Allah, and that our ultimate goal should be to seek His pleasure and contentment.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir, Al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah, Vol. 6, p. 190 The name Zaidun carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Zaid ibn Ali was the fifth caliph of the Umayyad Caliphate, ruling from 720 to 724 AD. Zaidun is believed to be one of his descendants.
